summary: An EEG validation script was updated to replace a random train/test split with a LOSO-style subject split and to replace an invalid contrastive loss implementation with a symmetric InfoNCE-style objective. datasets: Synthetic EEG toy dataset (5 subjects, 20 trials per subject)
lessons: Use subject-level splits for LOSO rather than random train/test splits.
Validate tensor dimensions to prevent runtime reduction errors.
Construct pairwise similarity matrices for InfoNCE instead of collapsing representations prematurely.
Treat temporal pooling as an explicit modeling assumption because it discards temporal information.
Avoid resetting the global random number generator inside reusable data-loading functions.
Toy synthetic datasets are useful for validation but are not substitutes for realistic EEG preprocessing or subject metadata.

summary: Implemented confidence-aware MatchNet support for the KUL pipeline while preserving the existing model interface. lessons: Preserve model forward() interfaces when extending research models to avoid downstream runtime regressions.

Document temporal pooling as an explicit modeling assumption because it discards temporal information.
Factor shared similarity computations into a single implementation to keep training and inference behavior consistent.
Validate any confidence-based decision thresholds on held-out LOSO subjects using calibration metrics before interpreting them as uncertainty estimates.

summary: Confidence-aware MatchNet support for the KUL pipeline was validated while preserving backward compatibility and the existing InfoNCE training methodology. task: Run 3.1 Frequency Pipeline Verification and Multi-Subject Smoke Test

summary: Attempted to implement a multi-subject interpretability smoke test for the KUL LOSO AAD-Conformer with quantitative FFT-based frequency validation, baseline verification, and cross-subject reporting. The run failed because cross-subject interpretability conclusions relied on unsupported heuristics, temporal and saliency consistency analyses did not answer the stated research question, and the required confidence-based orchestration pipeline was not implemented or verified.
lessons: Derive scientific conclusions only from executable analyses rather than heuristic thresholds or qualitative labels.
Compare subject-level interpretability outputs directly when assessing cross-subject consistency instead of measuring within-subject variability.
Evaluate temporal consistency using similarity of temporal occlusion profiles across subjects rather than dispersion of occlusion scores within each subject.
Evaluate saliency consistency using saliency values or channel rankings rather than vector dimensionality.
Treat frequency-ablation importance rankings as exploratory unless validated by an established methodology.
Clearly distinguish exploratory heuristics from validated scientific conclusions in generated reports.
Verification of cached signal spectral characteristics is not equivalent to verification of the upstream preprocessing pipeline.
Implement, execute, and record required orchestration pipelines before claiming workflow compliance.
Avoid recommending progression to subsequent experimental phases while blocking methodological validation issues remain unresolved.
Ensure every required deliverable is supported by executable evidence rather than inferred narrative.
